title: Grace: Graph Self-Distillation and Completion to Mitigate Degree-Related Biases

problem.claim: GNN-based node-classification methods perform poorly on low-degree nodes, creating a performance bottleneck in long-tailed real-world graphs.

gap.claim: Under-represented self-representations and low neighborhood homophily ratios are identified as the main causes of low-degree-node underperformance.

contributions.claim: Grace improves node representations through self-distillation.
Grace uses graph completion to increase the neighborhood homophily ratio of low-degree nodes.
Grace uses label propagation to mitigate error propagation from graph completion.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present Grace as a novel method.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that Grace supports real-world graphs and is superior in balancing degree-related bias and overall node-classification performance.

narrative_sequence.summary: Node classification is important across many real-world applications because graph data is broadly used.
GNN-based methods depend heavily on rich connections and perform poorly on low-degree nodes, which are common in long-tailed graphs.
The authors attribute the issue to under-represented self-representations and low neighborhood homophily ratios among low-degree nodes.
Grace applies self-distillation, graph completion, and label propagation to improve representations, increase neighborhood homophily, and limit error propagation.
The authors report favorable results on real-world graphs and improved balance between degree-related bias and overall performance.

source_observation.claim: Low-degree nodes suffer from weak self-representations and low neighborhood homophily.

interpretation.claim: Degree-related performance disparities may arise from both representation insufficiency and neighborhood quality.

application.claim: When addressing graph-model bias, consider jointly improving node representations and neighborhood structure.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether these interventions generalize beyond the reported real-world graph settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not describe the self-distillation, graph-completion, or label-propagation procedures in detail.
The abstract does not report computational cost, limitations, or failure cases.
